The math nobody shows renters

Let's do the math your landlord hopes you never do

Rent feels “safe” because there's no down payment. But look at what five years of it actually costs you — and what you own at the end of it.

$2,400/mo rent
= $144,000

That's five years of typical rent paid to a landlord. Gone. Every dollar of it. It never comes back and it never builds you a cent of equity.

  • ✕ $144,000 paid
  • ✕ $0 equity built
  • ✕ Nothing to show for it in year 6
Owning flips the math.

Your payment starts building your equity instead of your landlord's. And with assistance, getting in may cost less than a few months of rent.

  • ✓ $500–$5,000 typical out-of-pocket after assistance
  • ✓ Every payment builds your position

Myth vs. reality

Most buyers disqualify themselves based on lies

The things holding most renters back aren't true anymore. Here's what actually applies:

Myth
“I need 20% down.”

Reality
You don't. Many buyers get in with $500–$5,000 out of pocket once down payment assistance is applied — assistance can cover most of the down payment and sometimes part of closing costs too.

Myth
“My credit isn't good enough.”

Reality
Programs exist for buyers with scores in the low 600s. Below that today? My loan partner will map out exactly what to fix and how long it should take.

Myth
“Assistance is only for certain people.”

Reality
There are state, county, and lender programs with different rules — income limits, first-time buyer definitions, purchase areas. The only way to know which ones fit you is to run the application. It costs nothing to check.

Myth
“I should wait until I save more.”

Reality
Every month of rent is money that builds someone else's equity. Decide with real figures — not guesses.

Objections — answered straight

Before you talk yourself out of it…

The questions I hear most from first-time buyers:

How much money do I actually need saved?

Less than you think. With down payment assistance applied, many of the buyers I work with get into a home with $500–$5,000 out of pocket. Your exact number depends on the programs you qualify for — the application is how we find out. You can also book a free 15-minute call and ask me anything before you apply.

What credit score do I need?

Several programs work with scores in the low 600s. If you're under that, you're not out — my loan partner will tell you exactly what to address and give you a timeline, so you're working toward buying instead of guessing.

What is the $1,000 closing gift?

Buyers who close on a home with me in 2026 receive a $1,000 gift toward closing. It's my way of helping with the last stretch of costs — on top of whatever assistance programs you qualify for.

How long does the whole process take?

Typically 60–90 days from application to keys: pre-approval, home search, then escrow. That's exactly why starting now matters if you want to be in your home in early 2026.

Does applying cost anything or obligate me?

No. The application is how my loan partner checks which programs you qualify for. There's no cost and no obligation — you get your numbers and decide from there.

The worst move is guessing.
